description: Live-broadcast FilterBar + the two headline storytelling sections: the hero scatter (Headline Chart) and the two side-by-side Leaderboards. Depends on FEAT-001 (types, toe/stories logic, DashboardProvider/useDashboard). These are the first on-air talking-point surfaces.
steps: Create src/components/FilterBar.tsx: a sticky top bar (dark, high-contrast, big tactile controls) with a Week selector (weeks present in data), Position toggle (WR/TE/RB/All), Coverage toggle (Man/Zone/All), and a 'Current Game' matchup quick filter whose options are the gameIds/matchups available in the selected week. All controls write to DashboardProvider filter state via useDashboard().

Create src/components/HeadlineChart.tsx: Recharts ScatterChart, x=Open Rate (0-1), y=Target Share (0-1), reading the filtered dataset from useDashboard(). Color/shape split for Man vs Zone with a local toggle (uses targetShareVsMan/targetShareVsZone + openRateVsMan/openRateVsZone when a coverage view is active, else overall). Add a thick diagonal expectation ReferenceLine driven by expectedTargetShare(openRate). Render large bold player-name labels on ONLY the top 3-4 over-targeted (highest positive toe, above the line) and top 3-4 ignored (lowest negative toe, below the line) using toe() from src/lib/toe.ts. Hover <Tooltip> shows TOE, team, routesRun, targets, receptions. Default static view must tell the story with zero interaction.

Create src/components/Leaderboards.tsx: two always-visible side-by-side panels. Left 'Most Over-Targeted' = top 10 by positive TOE; right 'Most Ignored / Coach I Was Open' = top 10 by negative TOE, both computed from the filtered dataset. Each row: large bold player name + team badge + big TOE value (signed, colored) + one-line hook from deriveStoryHook(). Handle empty-filter state gracefully.

Wire FilterBar, HeadlineChart, and Leaderboards into a temporary dev view in app/page.tsx (wrapped in DashboardProvider) just enough to render and smoke-test them; final composition/layout happens in FEAT-004 but these must render now.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` exits 0 with no errors.

A short-lived `npm run dev` smoke check shows the scatter with a diagonal expectation line and large bold labels only on the ~3-4 extreme over-targeted and ~3-4 extreme ignored players, and no console/hydration errors.
Both leaderboards render 10 rows each (or fewer with a graceful message if the filter yields fewer) with name + team + TOE + a derived story hook.
Changing the Week, Position, Coverage, and Game filters visibly changes the scatter points and leaderboard rows.
verification: Short-lived dev check: start `npm run dev` in the background, wait ~5s, confirm the page compiles and renders the scatter + leaderboards with no runtime/hydration errors, then STOP the dev server (never leave it running).
findings:
COMPLETED. Built the three FEAT-002 surfaces, all client components reading useDashboard().

=== FILES ADDED ===
- src/components/FilterBar.tsx: sticky top bar (z-30, backdrop-blur, dark panel bg). Week <select> (availableWeeks(rows); changing week resets gameId to 'all'), Position segmented control (All/WR/TE/RB), Coverage segmented control (All/Man/Zone), Current Game <select> scoped by availableGames(rows, filters.week) with readable 'TEAM vs OPP' labels, and a Reset button -> resetFilters(). Active segment = bg-accent/text-ink; all writes go through setFilters(partial).
- src/components/HeadlineChart.tsx: Recharts ScatterChart in a 560px ResponsiveContainer. x=Open Rate (0-1), y=Target Share (0,'auto'), both tick-formatted as %. Thick diagonal expectation line via <ReferenceLine segment=[{x:0,y:expectedTargetShareLine(0,model)},{x:1,y:expectedTargetShareLine(1,model)}] stroke #facc15 width 3 dashed>, driven by the file's expectationModel (falls back to defaultModel when null). Two <Scatter> series split by sign of row.toe: over-targeted = pos/cyan, ignored = neg/rose. Local Overall/Man/Zone toggle swaps point coords to openRateVs*/targetShareVs*; it initializes from and follows filters.coverage via useEffect but can be overridden on the chart. Large bold name labels (last name, 16px weight 800, colored by sign) render ONLY on top-4 +TOE and top-4 -TOE via a custom <ExtremeLabel> Scatter label; all other points unlabelled. Custom <Tooltip> shows name, team, position, signed TOE, open %, target-share %, routes/targets/receptions.
- src/components/Leaderboards.tsx: two side-by-side panels (grid lg:grid-cols-2). Left 'Most Over-Targeted' top 10 by positive TOE (desc), right 'Most Ignored / Coach I Was Open' top 10 by negative TOE (asc). Each row: rank, large bold playerName, team badge, big signed/colored TOE %, and deriveStoryHook(row) one-liner. Empty-filter state shows a graceful message per panel.

=== KEY DECISION: per-player reduction ===
The real data is per-player-per-week (weeks 1-8), so with week='all' a player has up to 8 rows. All three visual surfaces (scatter + both leaderboards) reduce the filtered rows to ONE representative row per playerId = the week with the largest |toe| (same approach stories.ts selectTopNarratives uses), so a player appears once and the 'extremes' are real extremes, not duplicate weeks. toe/expectedTargetShare are READ FROM THE ROW per FEAT-001's contract; expectedTargetShareLine(a,b) is used ONLY for the diagonal reference line.

=== WIRING ===
app/page.tsx unchanged (already wraps DashboardShell in DashboardProvider). app/DashboardShell.tsx replaced its FEAT-001 placeholder body with <FilterBar/> + <HeadlineChart/> + <Leaderboards/> (keeps loading/error handling). This is the temporary dev composition; final layout + remaining sections land in later feats.

=== VERIFICATION (all pass) ===
npm run build exits 0, no type/lint errors (route / = 109kB, 212kB first load). Short-lived dev smoke check: started next dev detached, polled http://localhost:3000/ -> HTTP 200 (~16.5KB HTML), dev log shows 'Compiled / in 11.6s' and 'GET / 200' with an EMPTY stderr (no runtime/hydration/console errors), then STOPPED the server and confirmed port 3000 is free (had to kill the child next-server PID explicitly as Stop-Process on the npm parent didn't cascade). Recharts 2.x + React 18 render the SVG fine. Committed locally; NOT pushed.
